summary.text: James Ramos, a member of the Serrano/Cahuilla tribe and a lifelong resident of the San Manuel Indian Reservation, became the first California Native American state lawmaker in 2018. He represents the 45th Assembly District, which includes Fontana, Highland, Redlands, Rialto and San Bernardino.

paragraphs.text: He served on the San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors, including as board chair from 2015 to 2017, and is a former chairman of the San Manuel Band of Mission Indians.
Ramos earned an associate degree in business at Victor Valley College, a bachelor's degree in accounting at California State University, San Bernardino, and an MBA from the University of Redlands.
